art_instructions: Outside the village school, show the white‑washed building with blue wooden trim and a terracotta tile roof, a wooden‑post porch, and bright sunny light. An olive tree and a splash of bougainvillea frame the garden; a small stone bird bath sits near the entrance. In the foreground at center-left, Owl stands at child eye height on the stone path beside the same low, flat gray stone where the mice were seen. She has mottled brown-and-cream feathers, round amber eyes, a small green scarf tied at her neck, and a tiny satchel across her side. Her posture shows no fear: chest lifted, calm eyes, a slight confident smile, and wings slightly open for balance. She is eating the two mice: one small gray mouse is in her beak as she tilts her head back to swallow, with only the tail and back feet peeking out (no gore), while her right talon lightly holds the second mouse on the flat stone, ready to pick it up next. Keep other animals out of frame; you may show faint footprints on the dusty path leading away. Midday sun creates short, crisp shadows toward the viewer, and colors match the palette (Mediterranean blue trim, sunset-orange tiles, olive-green leaves).
